title: American Red Cross used Facebook's machine-learning population maps to focus Malawi mapping for the June 2017 measles vaccination campaign (Measles & Rubella Initiative)
summary: Facebook's ML settlement maps cut Red Cross mapping for Malawi's June 2017 measles vaccination campaign (Measles & Rubella Initiative) from 94,080 km² to 2,745 km²
account: For Malawi's June 2017 measles vaccination campaign (Measles & Rubella Initiative), targeting more than 7.5 million children, the American Red Cross's Missing Maps team needed base maps for campaign monitoring. Facebook's population maps, generated by a machine-learning computer-vision method that detects buildings in satellite imagery, were used to identify where people lived and which areas were already mapped in OpenStreetMap. Concentrating volunteers on settlements filtered out 97.1% of the land area, reducing the area to map from 94,080 km² to 2,745 km² and completing the base map in a fraction of the normal time. The base map was to feed a dashboard for government and Red Cross monitors during the campaign; the article predates the campaign and reports no monitoring outcome. No vaccination-coverage outcome attributable to the maps is reported. The date given is the Red Cross publication date.
purpose: Produce high-resolution population and settlement maps from satellite imagery for planning and humanitarian use.
system: Facebook (Meta) High Resolution Settlement Layer population density maps
developer: Facebook Inc. with CIESIN, Columbia University, and the World Bank Development Data Group
deployer: American Red Cross (Missing Maps) supporting the Measles and Rubella Initiative campaign in Malawi
domain: Humanitarian mapping for immunization campaign support
taxonomy_note: Direct fit for the documented result. Benefit created or restored chosen because the source documents a dated, quantified result for an identified deployment (mapping area cut by 97.1% for a named campaign); the effect on vaccination coverage is not documented, so depths are modest.

ratings.reason: Unassessed: the source reports no outcome for the 7.5 million targeted children; any benefit is indirect and unquantified.
Mapping area reduced from 94,080 km² to 2,745 km² and the base map completed in a fraction of the normal time.
Unassessed: a supporting role in one national campaign whose coverage effect was not measured.

ai_role.statement: The Facebook settlement data determined where volunteer mapping effort went and which areas were skipped; the campaign itself was a Measles & Rubella Initiative effort supported by the American Red Cross and other partners, with monitors from the national government, and the Red Cross attributes efficiency, not coverage, to the maps. The Red Cross account is the implementing organization's and names only 'Facebook's population datasets', without mentioning machine learning; the identification with the High Resolution Settlement Layer and the machine-learning description are taken from the vendor-authored Tiecke et al. preprint, which does not mention the Malawi campaign.
